This is also an issue on the n3iwf, when it is connected to an amf is uses 100% cpu

Hi, I also confirm that this happens with *n3iwf*, *amf* and *upfd*. Important to mention that my kernel is *5.3.0-26-generic*, not the exact one mentioned on the readme. However, the gtp driver compilation was successful so I didn't change it. Not sure if this is the issue.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6465668/82747842-af1e2180-9dcf-11ea-904c-6e0208c9a674.png)

As mentioned by @bjoern-r, everything seems normal on each component log window but CPU is 100%. In fact, just 
executing UPFD already yield this issue.
This seems to be scpt package's problem. But we're not in sure.
@free5gc-org has there been any update on this?

hi @endrigoshi @Matheus-Garbelini @bjoern-r ,

How about trying to use origin [sctp package](https://github.com/ishidawataru/sctp) instead of [this one](https://git.cs.nctu.edu.tw/calee/sctp)?

Maybe we can test to replace `git.cs.nctu.edu.tw/calee/sctp` with `github.com/ishidawataru/sctp` and check if it fix the problem.

I ran a quick test and the CPU utilization of AMF was in reasonable intervals, somewhat in the range of 7-15%.
I would say that the problem is resolved by using the original library, but in case I notice it again I will let you know.

Hi @free5gc-org ,

This bug is still persistent in the latest version of the Core network. Given this, why not switch to the older library [https://github.com/ishidawataru/sctp](https://github.com/ishidawataru/sctp) until this issue is resolved? 
Including the test files, there are like 10 files in total where the replacement needs to be performed, so not a great overhead I suppose.
@bjoern-r @Matheus-Garbelini @endrigoshi What UE did you use to connect to the n3iwf?
